description:
We are a team interested in space exploration, Earth science, and technology. Our goal is to build an interactive solution that identifies Earth locations that resemble Moon and Mars environments using NASA data.
We are looking for teammates interested in data analysis, satellite data, mapping, 3D visualization, and design to help us create an engaging and informative project.
summary:
**Mars Analog Explorer** is an interactive research platform designed to explore how Earth environments can serve as analogs for studying Mars. The project compares three locations: the Atacama Desert in Chile, Wadi Rum in Jordan, and Gale Crater on Mars.

We developed a platform that brings together scientific research, environmental datasets, maps, visualizations, and interactive comparison tools. It allows users to explore similarities and differences between these environments using available thermal, elevation, and surface data.

The project addresses the challenge by helping researchers and space exploration enthusiasts understand which specific characteristics of Earth environments can support the study and preparation of future planetary missions. Rather than claiming that any location on Earth perfectly represents Mars, the platform highlights both similarities and scientific limitations.

This project is important because studying Earth’s extreme environments can help scientists test ideas, understand planetary processes, and prepare technologies and strategies for future exploration of Mars and other planetary bodies.
details: > Project Terra X is an interactive research tool that explores how selected Earth sites can inform Mars-analogue studies. It presents the Atacama Desert and Wadi Rum alongside Mars observations of Gale Crater through maps, site profiles, report figures, measurements, comparisons, and mission-planning recommendations. The project uses NASA ASTER temperature, reflectance, and elevation data, as well as THEMIS and MOLA context for Gale Crater. Each finding is linked to its source and limitations. Instead of assigning an unsupported similarity score, the tool highlights differences in measurements, units, scale, and reference systems. A separate module presents lunar data without mixing it into the Mars comparison. The project was built with React, TypeScript, Vite, Leaflet, and Three.js. AI tools assisted with code and some explanatory text; no AI-generated measurements or images were used. Project Terra X is a research and planning aid, not a site certification or substitute for field validation.
